title: Ad-hoc ensemble eval playback lab
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad for an evening playthrough of ad‑hoc ensemble/fallback behavior. This is a personal lab doc — messy, leaning on heuristics rather than formal metrics. Goal: capture sharp failure modes and quick rubric so we can triage whether a rollback / hotfix / probe is needed.

1) Context and why I care
- Running a short pulse test of the new ensemble routing that prefers quantized small-model fallback under high-latency tails. Wanted to see conversational coherency and truthfulness when route shifts mid-session.
- Test inputs are a 40-example mini-suite (mixed Q/A, follow-up clarifications, code completion). Samples drawn from customer-reported regressions + seeded adversarial prompts.

2) Tiny ad-hoc rubric (0–3, integer scores)\- Relevance: 0 none / 1 partial / 2 mostly / 3 on-target\- Coherence: 0 broken / 1 shifty / 2 generally coherent / 3 crisp follow-through\- Hallucination: 0 hallucinated facts / 1 some unsupported claims / 2 minor errors / 3 grounded\- Latency surprise: 0 >1.5s extra / 1 0.8–1.5s extra / 2 <0.8s extra / 3 no noticeable penalty
Notes: scoring intentionally coarse to speed annotation. I assign worst-case where model switches mid-answer.

3) Interesting samples / observations (representative)
- Sample A (multi-turn FAQ -> clarifying question): baseline-hosted v1.7 produced clear clarifying Q then followed with short relevant answer (scores: R3 C3 H3 L3). Ensemble-run (small fallback triggered on token 92) produced the clarifying Q but then truncated continuation and repeated an earlier clause -> (R2 C1 H2 L2). Hypothesis: KV-cache continuity broken when routing jumps to quantized variant that lacks identical tokenization or head alignment.

- Sample B (code completion, Python snippet): fallback returned syntactically valid but semantically wrong API usage (used deprecated signature). Human-impact: medium. Scores: (R2 C2 H1 L3). Observation: quantized small model weights likely trained on older snapshot leading to stale code patterns. Link to failing trace: github PR above.

- Sample C (factual multi-hop): when ensemble switched in the middle of step 2, the model dropped a necessary intermediate reasoning step and asserted a conclusion (hallucination). Scores: (R1 C1 H0 L1). This is high risk for customers that rely on chain-of-thought consistency.

4) Regression signal summary vs baseline (hosted v1.7)\- Out of 40 examples: 9 degraded noticeably (score delta >= -2 overall), 27 comparable, 4 marginally better (edge lexical cases).\- Degradation concentrated in multi-turn and code examples, not single-shot summarization.\- Timing: most switches occur on long-tail tokens (token index > 60) during decoder flush / batch boundary.

5) Quick hypotheses (ranked)
- Hypothesis 1: KV cache transfer incomplete when routing to quantized variant (token offsets or attention cache shape mismatch) -> leads to truncation/repetition.
- Hypothesis 2: Quantized small model snapshot predates code corpus updates -> returns older API patterns.
- Hypothesis 3: Tokenization differences (byte-level vs whitespace normalization) between variants cause misalignment mid-sequence.
- Hypothesis 4: Routing policy allows fallback mid-answer under load; we should prefer per-message boundary routing for long-lived chats.

6) Quick mitigation ideas (experiment plans)
- Reproduce locally with deterministic seed, log KV shapes and token offsets at route time. Add more aggressive assertions in runtime to catch cache-shape drift.
- Try a policy change: do not allow fallback if (current_sequence_length > 64) OR (is_multiturn = true). Run A/B for 8hr window.
- Replace small-model snapshot with latest quantized build that includes recent code corpus, then rerun smoke.
- Add a short sanity-check micro-eval post-route: feed last n tokens through candidate model and compare next-token logits for divergence threshold; if diverges > X, route back or regenerate.

7) Concrete next steps (my TODOs)
- [ ] Add a lightweight probe to serving runtime that emits KV-cache metadata on route events (ticket JIRA-9876).
- [ ] Re-run the 40-example suite with token-level traces exported (Felix -> Maya pairing).
- [ ] Draft quick blurb for eng-channel summarizing risk and suggested policy tweak (Ibrahim to review).
- [ ] If confirmed, propose immediate policy temp-fix: disable mid-sequence fallback for chat routes.

8) Open questions / things to watch
- What is the expected cost increase if we turn off mid-sequence fallback during heavy load? Need cost vs reliability numbers.
- Can we adopt a lightweight cache-compatibility fingerprint so we can fast-verify candidate models are safe to continue from an existing cache?
- Are there customer contracts that could be impacted by disabling fallback (SLA burst capacity expectations)? Loop in CS if needed.

9) Random notes / scribbles
- Observed one case where repeat token pattern was identical to a known tokenizer split artifact (see sample A). Might be a quick win.
- If we automate a sanity-check that costs ~1–2ms/token, that may still be cheaper than user-facing hallucination incidents.

End of scratch. Will iterate once I have token traces. Keep this doc as ephemeral; if we formalize, migrate to confluence and link back.
